question.problem:
Given that $f(x)=\frac{x}{6+x-{x}^{2}},$ which of the following statements is correct?

I. ${lim}_{x\to (-2)^{-}}f(x)=-\infty $

II. ${lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}f(x)=-\infty $

III. ${lim}_{x\to (-2)}f(x)=\text{DNE}$
question.worked_solution:
First, we note that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x}{6+x-{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{x}{(x-3)(x+2)}.\end{aligned}
$$

This implies that the function $f(x)=\frac{x}{6+x-{x}^{2}}$ has two vertical asymptotes $x=-2$ and $x=3.$

To compute the one-sided limits as $x\to (-2),$ we evaluate $f(x)$ at $x$-values very close to $x=-2$ from the right and from the left.

| $x$ | $-2.01$ | $-2.001$ | $-2$ | $-1.999$ | $-1.99$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $≈40.12$ | $≈400.12$ | $\text{undefined}$ | $≈-399.88$ | $≈-39.88$ |

All values are positive and get larger and larger as $x\to (-2)$ from the left and all values are negative and get smaller and smaller as $x\to (-2)$ from the right. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{-}}f(x)=+\infty ,\,\,\,{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}f(x)=-\infty .
$$

Consequently, statement I is false and II is true.

Finally, since both left and right-sided limits at $x=-2$ are different, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-2)}f(x)=\text{DNE},
$$

and therefore III is also true.

In conclusion, only statements II and III are true. A plot of the function is shown below.
